evidence.reason: The close handler is the only place that unregisters cleanup, clears the timer, removes the abort listener, and settles the run. The exit handler merely records exitedCleanly and does not finalize. A detached descendant that inherits stdout/stderr can keep those pipes open after the original process group is killed, so Node may not emit close; then a timeout or cancellation leaves the run pending indefinitely instead of settling. This is an ordinary implementation defect in intended timeout/cancellation behavior. The smallest fix is bounded post-termination finalization that removes hooks, closes capture streams, and settles once, using the recorded exit code when available.
